title: House committee advances Davidson's American Lending Fairness Act of 2026
text:
House committee advances Davidson’s American Lending Fairness Act of 2026
N. E. Stubbs
The House Financial Services Committee passed Representative Warren Davidson’s American Lending Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 7866) on Sep. 16, legislation that aims to prevent states from applying their own interest rate limits to loans made by banks and credit unions chartered in other states.
"Borrowers should be free to shop for whatever loan works best for them, regardless of which state the lender is chartered in,” said Warren Davidson. “My American Lending Fairness Act protects that freedom by putting state-chartered banks and credit unions on equal footing with the largest national banks. When more lenders compete for business, borrowers get better rates. I'm proud to see this bill move forward, and I look forward to a full House vote."
The bill addresses ongoing disputes over sections of the Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act of 1980 (DIDMCA), particularly Section 521 and Section 525. Section 521 allows FDIC-insured, state-chartered banks to charge interest rates permitted in their home state or a specified federal alternative, even if those rates conflict with another state's usury caps. Section 525 permits states to opt out of these rules for loans "made in" that state.
A key issue has been how courts interpret where a loan is "made in," whether based on the bank's location, lending activity, or the borrower's location. This definition determines if a state's DIDMCA opt-out can limit an out-of-state bank's interest rate when lending to residents within its borders.
Davidson’s bill proposes eliminating DIDMCA’s current opt-out framework under Section 525 and would allow states only to cap rates charged by institutions they charter—not those chartered elsewhere but lending into their state.
Warren Davidson currently serves as U.S. Representative for Ohio’s 8th district after replacing John Boehner in 2016; he was born in Sidney, Ohio in 1970 and lives in Troy, according to the official congressional website.
